Surgeon.notes: Four of the six jacks are unnamed in the source and show no tooltip: the X, Y and Z jacks and the freeze jack. The panel letters them X, Y, Z, a snowflake, V/OCT and TRIG. The default expressions on a fresh module are 0 for j, k, l and the time warp, 0.0039 for the attack, 0.5 for the decay, i*f for the pitch, 1/i*e for the amplitude and 1 for the phase; a phase expression of exactly 0 stops the phase being reset on a trigger. CLatch.notes: The tolerance control is a latching lamp button configured with three values, so each click steps to the next of 1ms, 16ms and 64ms and then wraps. src/CLatch.cpp:65 queues a falling change whenever an input reads zero and has not moved, which is the state of an unpatched jack, so empty rows are driven low rather than left alone. lines: Four independent curve generators sharing one time base, each with its own end-of-cycle trigger, and a running sum and trigger stream taken from whichever of them are not patched out
Starts that segment from the beginning; it fires on any rise in voltage
Cycles the shape of that segment through up, down, up-down, down-up and a held constant; the lamp reads red, green, orange, blue and white in that order
Sets how long that segment takes, as a multiplier on the module's time scale: a quarter at the far left, one at centre and sixteen times at the far right
Sets how much of the segment is played before it stops, all of it at the far right and a shorter fragment as it is turned down; the fragment takes the whole time set for the segment
Sets how many triggers are spread through that segment, 1 to 8
Bends the shape of that segment away from straight lines, symmetrical at centre; for the held constant shape this knob sets the value that is held instead
Scales the height of that segment, silent at the far left, unity at centre and double at the far right
A 10V pulse the moment that segment finishes, whether it ran to its end or stopped short
That segment's own curve, five volts at full height and scaled by its amp knob; patching this jack takes the segment out of the module's running and trig outputs
A trigger here resets the running output to zero and stops all four segments
Sets the time every segment is measured against, 64 milliseconds at the far left to about a second at the far right
Chooses how the triggers are spread through a segment: down, they are spaced evenly in time; up, they are spaced evenly up the segment's height, so a steep part fires them faster
The running total of every segment not patched out at its own jack, held between -10V and 10V; it sums their movements rather than their values, so it drifts and stays where it is left
A 10V pulse whenever any segment that is not patched out at its own jack fires one of its triggers
Note — Nothing moves until a trigger arrives at a segment's own trig jack; the segments do not free-run and the reset jack only stops them
Note — The module declares a scaled sum output that has no jack on the panel, so the running output is the only summed voltage available

Convection.notes: The four segments are lettered a, b, c and d on the panel and numbered 1 to 4 in the maker's tooltips. The panel prints T for a segment's trig input, EOC and E for its two outputs, LEN, a percent sign, DENS and SKEW for four of its knobs; the amp knob and the shape button carry no lettering. Output 10, 'Scaled sum CV', is configured in src/Convection.cpp:71 but no jack is added for it in the widget, so no click can reach it and it gets no line. The running output accumulates each segment's frame-to-frame movement rather than its value, so it holds its level between segments instead of returning to zero.

Spoon.notes: Spoon is work in progress. Its widget loads A Saw B's panel (src/Spoon.cpp:82), so the artwork and lettering are wrong; only on a theme change does step() try to load res/panels/Spoon.svg, which is not in the installed plugin. FEEDBACK_PARAM is placed on the panel at line 86 but is never passed to configParam and never read in process, so it is dead and has no tooltip. TRIG_IN is declared and read at line 65 but no jack is added for it, so no click can reach it and it gets no line here. The module browser's description, 'Variable hardness clipper', is copied from Plastic Wrap. The maker's manual has no section for this module. The Friction knob runs 0 to 10 and the Tension knob 0.8 to 12, both used as powers of two.
